subject: Chemistry
question_text: A solution of aluminium chloride is electrolysed for 30 minutes using a current of 2 A. The amount of the aluminium deposited at the cathode is ____. [Given: molar mass of aluminium and chlorine are 27 g mol$^{-1}$ and 35.5 g mol$^{-1}$ respectively, Faraday constant = 96500 C mol$^{-1}$]
problem_types: calculate mass deposited using w = (Eq. wt x I x t)/F
common_mistakes: Using equivalent weight = molar mass instead of molar mass/3 (since Al is trivalent)
Forgetting to convert minutes to seconds
prerequisite_concepts: w = (M x I x t)/(n x F)

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which of the following statements is not true for radioactive decay?

options.text: Amount of radioactive substance remained after three half lives is $\dfrac{1}{8}$th of original amount.
Decay constant does not depend upon temperature.
Decay constant increases with increase in temperature.
Half life is $\ln 2$ times of $\dfrac{1}{\text{rate constant}}$.

problem_types: identify incorrect statement about decay kinetics
common_mistakes: Confusing radioactive decay constant (temperature independent) with chemical reaction rate constants (Arrhenius dependence on temperature)
prerequisite_concepts: first order kinetics of radioactive decay
amount remaining after n half-lives = N0/2^n

subject: Chemistry
question_text: How many different stereoisomers are possible for the given molecule? $CH_3-CH(OH)-CH=CH-CH_3$
problem_types: count total stereoisomers combining geometrical (cis/trans) and optical (R/S) isomerism
common_mistakes: Counting only geometrical isomers and ignoring the chiral centre, or vice versa
Forgetting total stereoisomers = (number of geometrical isomers) x (number of optical configurations)
prerequisite_concepts: cis/trans isomerism about C=C double bond

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which of the following electronegativity order is incorrect?
problem_types: identify incorrect ordering of electronegativity among given elements
common_mistakes: Assuming electronegativity always increases left to right and decreases down a group without checking actual Pauling values, especially for Mg vs Al
prerequisite_concepts: Pauling electronegativity values of period 2 and 3 elements
general periodic trends (increase across a period, decrease down a group)

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Lanthanoid ions with $4f^7$ configuration are: (A) $Eu^{2+}$ (B) $Gd^{3+}$ (C) $Eu^{3+}$ (D) $Tb^{3+}$ (E) $Sm^{2+}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
problem_types: identify ions with 4f^7 configuration from given lanthanoid ions
common_mistakes: Forgetting that Gd3+ has configuration [Xe]4f^7 5d^0 6s^0 (since Gd is [Xe]4f^7 5d^1 6s^2 and loses 5d and 6s electrons)
Confusing Eu2+ (4f^7) with Eu3+ (4f^6)
prerequisite_concepts: ground state electronic configurations of lanthanides

subject: Chemistry
question_text:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I:
(A) $Al^{3+} < Mg^{2+} < Na^+ < F^-$
(B) $B < C < O < N$
(C) $B < Al < Mg < K$
(D) $Si < P < S < Cl$

List-II:
(I) Ionisation Enthalpy
(II) Metallic character
(III) Electronegativity
(IV) Ionic radii

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
problem_types: match orderings of elements/ions to the periodic property they represent
common_mistakes: Confusing ionisation enthalpy trend (B<C<O<N is an exception due to stable half-filled p3 configuration of N) with electronegativity trend
Mixing up metallic character and electronegativity trends across a period/group
prerequisite_concepts: isoelectronic species and ionic radii trend
anomalous ionisation enthalpy of N vs O
metallic character increases down a group/left across a period

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which of the following acids is a vitamin?
problem_types: identify vitamin from list of acids
common_mistakes: Confusing aspartic acid (an amino acid) with ascorbic acid (vitamin C)

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A liquid when kept inside a thermally insulated closed vessel at $25^\circ C$ was mechanically stirred from outside. What will be the correct option for the following thermodynamic parameters?
problem_types: determine signs of q, w and DeltaU for stirring in an insulated vessel
common_mistakes: Assuming q=0 implies DeltaU=0 (only true if w is also 0)
Sign convention confusion: work done ON the system by stirring is positive (w>0), increasing internal energy
prerequisite_concepts: mechanical stirring does work on the system

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Radius of the first excited state of Helium ion is given as: ($a_0 \to$ radius of the first stationary state of hydrogen atom).
problem_types: compute orbital radius of He+ in first excited state using r = a0 n^2/Z
common_mistakes: Using n=1 instead of n=2 for the 'first excited state'
Forgetting to divide by Z=2 for Helium ion
prerequisite_concepts: first excited state corresponds to n=2

subject: Chemistry
question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: $CH_3-O-CH_2-Cl$ will undergo $S_N1$ reaction though it is a primary halide.

Statement II: $(CH_3)_3C-CH_2-Cl$ will not undergo $S_N2$ reaction very easily though it is a primary halide.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

problem_types: assess feasibility of SN1/SN2 for given primary halides based on stability/sterics
common_mistakes: Assuming all primary halides only undergo SN2
Not recognizing that the oxocarbenium ion (CH3-O-CH2+) is highly stabilized by resonance, favouring SN1
Not recognizing steric hindrance of neopentyl chloride slows SN2
prerequisite_concepts: steric hindrance effect on SN2 rate (neopentyl halides)

subject: Chemistry
question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: One mole of propyne reacts with excess of sodium to liberate half a mole of $H_2$ gas.

Statement II: Four g of propyne reacts with $NaNH_2$ to liberate $NH_3$ gas which occupies 224 mL at STP.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

problem_types: verify stoichiometry of propyne reactions with Na and NaNH2
common_mistakes: Errors converting 4 g of propyne to moles (molar mass = 40 g/mol)
Errors converting moles of NH3 produced to volume at STP (22400 mL/mol)
prerequisite_concepts: terminal alkyne C-H is acidic and reacts with Na to release H2 (1:1/2 mole ratio)
reaction with NaNH2 releases NH3 in 1:1 mole ratio
molar volume of gas at STP = 22400 mL

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A vessel at 1000 K contains $CO_2$ with a pressure of 0.5 atm. Some of $CO_2$ is converted into CO on addition of graphite. If the total pressure at equilibrium is 0.8 atm, then $K_P$ is:
problem_types: set up equilibrium table for CO2(g)+C(s) <-> 2CO(g) and compute Kp
common_mistakes: Errors setting up the change in pressure x in terms of total pressure increase
Forgetting graphite (solid) does not appear in Kp expression
prerequisite_concepts: total pressure = sum of partial pressures at equilibrium

subject: Chemistry
question_text: The IUPAC name of the following compound is: $HOOC-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-COOCH_3$
problem_types: determine IUPAC name with carboxylic acid as principal characteristic group and ester as substituent
common_mistakes: Choosing the ester group as the principal characteristic group instead of the carboxylic acid (acid has higher priority than ester)
Incorrect numbering of the parent chain leading to wrong locants
prerequisite_concepts: seniority order of functional groups (acid > ester)
naming -COOCH3 as 'methoxycarbonyl' substituent when acid is the principal group

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Which of the following electrolyte can be used to obtain $H_2S_2O_8$ by the process of electrolysis?

options.text: Acidified dilute solution of sodium sulphate

problem_types: identify suitable electrolyte for preparation of H2S2O8 by electrolysis
common_mistakes: Choosing dilute solutions, which favour water oxidation (O2 evolution) at the anode rather than HSO4- oxidation
Confusing this preparation with that of other oxoacids of sulphur
prerequisite_concepts: high concentration of HSO4- needed to favour this oxidation over water oxidation

subject: Chemistry
question_text:
The compounds which give a positive Fehling's test are:
(A) Benzaldehyde (PhCHO)
(B) Phenylacetone (Ph-CH2-CO-CH3)
(C) $HOCH_2-CO-(CHOH)_3-CH_2-OH$
(D) Acetaldehyde ($CH_3-CHO$)
(E) Phenylacetaldehyde (Ph-CH2-CHO)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
problem_types: identify which compounds give positive Fehling's test
common_mistakes: Forgetting that aromatic aldehydes (like benzaldehyde) do NOT give a positive Fehling's test
Not recognizing the polyhydroxy ketone (C) as a reducing sugar-like structure that gives positive Fehling's test
prerequisite_concepts: Fehling's test is positive for aliphatic aldehydes and alpha-hydroxy ketones (reducing sugars), but negative for aromatic aldehydes and ketones without alpha-hydroxy groups

subject: Chemistry
question_text: In which of the following complexes the CFSE, $\Delta_0$ will be equal to zero?
problem_types: determine which complex has CFSE = 0 based on d-electron configuration and ligand field strength
common_mistakes: Not determining the correct oxidation state of Fe in each complex before assigning d-electron count
Forgetting CFSE=0 for high-spin d5 (t2g^3 eg^2) configuration since (-0.4x3+0.6x2)=0
prerequisite_concepts: oxidation state determination in coordination compounds
weak field (high spin) vs strong field (low spin) ligands
CFSE formula in terms of t2g and eg electron occupancy

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Colligative Properties - Elevation in Boiling Point
question_text:
Arrange the following solutions in order of their increasing boiling points.
(i) $10^{-4}$ M NaCl
(ii) $10^{-4}$ M Urea
(iii) $10^{-3}$ M NaCl
(iv) $10^{-2}$ M NaCl
problem_types: rank solutions by boiling point elevation considering van't Hoff factor i and concentration
common_mistakes: Forgetting NaCl dissociates into 2 ions (i=2) while urea does not dissociate (i=1)
Not computing effective concentration (i x C) for comparison
prerequisite_concepts: DeltaTb = i Kb m (proportional to i x C)
van't Hoff factor for NaCl=2, urea=1

subject: Chemistry
question_text:
The products formed in the following reaction sequence are:

Nitrobenzene $\xrightarrow{(i)\ Br_2/AcOH}$ $\xrightarrow{(ii)\ Sn, HCl}$ $\xrightarrow{(iii)\ NaNO_2, HCl, 273\,K}$ $\xrightarrow{(iv)\ C_2H_5OH}$ A + B
problem_types: trace a multi-step aromatic synthesis to identify two final products
common_mistakes: Forgetting bromination occurs para to the electron-withdrawing nitro group is actually meta-directed (NO2 is meta directing), so bromine ends up meta to NH2 after reduction
Forgetting C2H5OH reduces diazonium salt to benzene (releasing N2) while itself getting oxidized to acetaldehyde
prerequisite_concepts: NO2 is a meta-directing deactivating group
diazonium salt + ethanol gives the deamination product (replacement of N2+ by H) and acetaldehyde

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Geometry, Magnetic Behaviour and Oxidation State
question_text: From the magnetic behaviour of $[NiCl_4]^{2-}$ (paramagnetic) and $[Ni(CO)_4]$ (diamagnetic), choose the correct geometry and oxidation state.

options.text: $[NiCl_4]^{2-}$ : Ni$^{II}$, square planar; $[Ni(CO)_4]$ : Ni(0), square planar

problem_types: determine geometry and oxidation state of Ni in two complexes from given magnetic behaviour
common_mistakes: Assuming paramagnetic complexes are always square planar (sp3 tetrahedral complexes with unpaired electrons are also paramagnetic)
Forgetting Ni(CO)4 has Ni in zero oxidation state since CO is a neutral ligand
prerequisite_concepts: Ni2+ : [Ar]3d8, sp3 tetrahedral with 2 unpaired electrons (paramagnetic)
Ni(0): [Ar]3d10 4s0, sp3 tetrahedral, all electrons paired (diamagnetic)

subject: Chemistry
question_text:
The incorrect statements regarding geometrical isomerism are:
(A) Propene shows geometrical isomerism.
(B) Trans isomer has identical atoms/groups on the opposite sides of the double bond.
(C) Cis-but-2-ene has higher dipole moment than trans-but-2-ene.
(D) 2-methylbut-2-ene shows two geometrical isomers.
(E) Trans-isomer has lower melting point than cis isomer.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
problem_types: identify all incorrect statements among five about geometrical isomerism
common_mistakes: Forgetting propene (CH3-CH=CH2) cannot show GI as one carbon of the double bond has two identical H atoms
Forgetting 2-methylbut-2-ene also has two identical groups (two CH3) on one carbon, so it does not show GI
Confusing melting point trend: trans isomers generally have HIGHER melting points than cis (more symmetric, better packing), so statement E is incorrect
prerequisite_concepts: condition for geometrical isomerism (each doubly bonded carbon must have two different substituents)
dipole moment comparison of cis vs trans isomers

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Some $CO_2$ gas was kept in a sealed container at a pressure of 1 atm and at 273 K. This entire amount of $CO_2$ gas was later passed through an aqueous solution of $Ca(OH)_2$. The excess unreacted $Ca(OH)_2$ was later neutralized with 0.1 M of 40 mL HCl. If the volume of the sealed container of $CO_2$ was x, then x is ____ $cm^3$ (nearest integer). [Given: The entire amount of $CO_2(g)$ reacted with exactly half the initial amount of $Ca(OH)_2$ present in the aqueous solution.]
problem_types: combine gas law with titration stoichiometry to find volume of CO2 container
common_mistakes: Errors converting mL HCl and molarity into moles of HCl and then to gram equivalents of Ca(OH)2
Forgetting that CO2 reacted with only half the initial Ca(OH)2, so total Ca(OH)2 = 2 x (moles of CO2)
prerequisite_concepts: ideal gas equation / molar volume at STP
gram equivalent concept for acid-base neutralization

subject: Chemistry
question_text: In Carius method for estimation of halogens, 180 mg of an organic compound produced 143.5 mg of AgCl. The percentage composition of chlorine in the compound is ____ %. [Given: molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ of Ag: 108, Cl = 35.5]
problem_types: compute percentage of halogen from mass of AgCl precipitate
common_mistakes: Using molar mass of AgCl incorrectly (should be 143.5 g/mol)
Forgetting to express the final answer as a percentage of the 180 mg sample
prerequisite_concepts: moles of Cl = moles of AgCl
%Cl = (mass of Cl / mass of compound) x 100

subject: Chemistry
question_text:
The number of molecules/ions that show linear geometry among the following is ____.
$SO_2, BeCl_2, CO_2, N_3^-, NO_2, F_2O, XeF_2, NO_2^+, I_3^-, O_3$
problem_types: determine geometry of each species using VSEPR and count linear ones
common_mistakes: Forgetting XeF2 and I3- are linear due to sp3d hybridization with lone pairs occupying equatorial positions
Including bent molecules like SO2, NO2, F2O, O3 which have a lone pair causing bent geometry
prerequisite_concepts: VSEPR theory for AXn type molecules
effect of lone pairs on molecular shape
hybridization (sp, sp2, sp3d) of central atoms

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Arrhenius Equation and First Order Kinetics
question_text: $A \to B$. The molecule A changes into its isomeric form B by following a first order kinetics at a temperature of 1000 K. If the energy barrier with respect to reactant energy for such isomeric transformation is 191.48 kJ mol$^{-1}$ and the frequency factor is $10^{20}$, the time required for 50% molecules of A to become B is ____ picoseconds (nearest integer). [$R = 8.314\,JK^{-1}mol^{-1}$]
problem_types: compute rate constant from Arrhenius equation then find half-life and convert units
common_mistakes: Errors evaluating $e^{-Ea/RT}$, especially converting to base-10 exponent (Ea/RT = 23.03 = ln10 x 10)
Forgetting to convert the final half-life from seconds to picoseconds (multiply by 10^12)

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Diazonium Salt Reactions - Sandmeyer and Wurtz-Fittig
question_text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions:

Nitrobenzene $\xrightarrow{(i)\ Sn + HCl}$ $\xrightarrow{(ii)\ NaNO_2, HCl, 0^\circ C}$ $\xrightarrow{(iii)\ Cu_2Cl_2}$ $\xrightarrow{(iv)\ Na, Ether}$ A (Product)

Molar mass of the product formed (A) is ____ g mol$^{-1}$.
problem_types: trace a multi-step synthesis to final product and compute its molar mass
common_mistakes: Not recognizing Cu2Cl2 converts the diazonium salt to chlorobenzene (Sandmeyer reaction)
Not recognizing Na/ether on chlorobenzene (Wurtz-Fittig/Fittig type coupling) gives biphenyl
prerequisite_concepts: NaNO2/HCl at 0C forms a diazonium salt
Fittig reaction: 2 ArCl + Na -> Ar-Ar (biphenyl, M=154 g/mol)

subject: Mathematics
question_text: The number of non-empty equivalence relations on the set $\{1, 2, 3\}$ is:
problem_types: counting relations
common_mistakes: Forgetting that the diagonal relation must always be included
Miscounting partitions of a 3-element set

subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Functional Equations and Area Under Curves
question_text: Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f(x+y) = f(x)f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$. If $f'(0) = 4a$ and $f$ satisfies $f''(x) - 3a f'(x) - f(x) = 0$, $a > 0$, then the area of the region $R = \{(x,y) \mid 0 \le y \le f(ax), 0 \le x \le 2\}$ is:
problem_types: derive function form from functional equation then integrate
common_mistakes: Wrong sign while solving the auxiliary quadratic for lambda
Substituting wrong value of a into f(ax) before integrating
prerequisite_concepts: second order linear ODE with constant coefficients

subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Reflection of a Point/Triangle in a Line
question_text: Let the triangle PQR be the image of the triangle with vertices $(1,3)$, $(3,1)$ and $(2,4)$ in the line $x + 2y = 2$. If the centroid of $\triangle PQR$ is the point $(\alpha, \beta)$, then $15(\alpha - \beta)$ is equal to:
concept_tags: reflection of a point in a line
problem_types: image of centroid under reflection
common_mistakes: Reflecting each vertex individually instead of reflecting the centroid directly (image of centroid = centroid of image)
Sign errors in the reflection formula
prerequisite_concepts: formula for image of a point in a line ax+by+c=0

subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Complex Numbers on the Unit Circle
question_text: Let $z_1, z_2, z_3$ be three complex numbers on the circle $|z| = 1$ with $\arg(z_1) = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $\arg(z_2) = 0$ and $\arg(z_3) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$. If $|z_1\bar{z_2} + z_2\bar{z_3} + z_3\bar{z_1}|^2 = \alpha + \beta\sqrt{2}$, $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{Z}$, then the value of $\alpha^2 + \beta^2$ is:
problem_types: evaluate modulus of sum of complex exponentials
common_mistakes: Sign errors in subtracting arguments while computing conjugates
Errors expanding $|a+bi|^2$

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Using the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, the sum of the maximum and the minimum values of $16\left((\sec^{-1}x)^2 + (\text{cosec}^{-1}x)^2\right)$ is:
problem_types: optimize a function using sec^-1 x + cosec^-1 x = pi/2 identity
common_mistakes: Using the wrong range/domain for sec^-1 and cosec^-1
Forgetting that x cannot lie in (-1,1)
prerequisite_concepts: completing the square for quadratic optimization

subject: Mathematics
question_text: A coin is tossed three times. Let X denote the number of times a tail follows a head. If $\mu$ and $\sigma^2$ denote the mean and variance of X, then the value of $64(\mu + \sigma^2)$ is:
concept_tags: mean and variance of random variable
problem_types: enumerate sample space to build probability distribution
common_mistakes: Miscounting the number of 'tail follows head' patterns in HTH, THT etc.
Errors computing variance = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ be a G.P. of increasing positive terms. If $a_1 a_5 = 28$ and $a_2 + a_4 = 29$, then $a_6$ is equal to:
problem_types: find GP term using product and sum conditions
common_mistakes: Choosing the decreasing root for r since the GP is increasing
Arithmetic slip while computing a6 = ar^5
prerequisite_concepts: solving simultaneous equations involving a and r

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let $L_1: \dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y-2}{3} = \dfrac{z-3}{4}$ and $L_2: \dfrac{x-2}{3} = \dfrac{y-4}{4} = \dfrac{z-5}{5}$ be two lines. Then which of the following points lies on the line of the shortest distance between $L_1$ and $L_2$?
problem_types: find the line of shortest distance and check a point on it
common_mistakes: Errors setting up direction ratios of the common perpendicular PQ
Sign mistakes while solving the two perpendicularity equations
prerequisite_concepts: condition of perpendicularity using direction ratios
equation of a line through two points

subject: Mathematics
question_text: The product of all solutions of the equation $e^{5(\log_e x)^2 + 3} = x^8$, $x > 0$, is:
problem_types: solve exponential equation by taking log and forming quadratic
common_mistakes: Forgetting to take ln on both sides correctly
Confusing product of roots of the quadratic in t=ln x with product of x-values directly without exponentiating sum of roots
prerequisite_concepts: sum/product of roots of a quadratic

subject: Mathematics
question_text: If $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n} T_r = \dfrac{(2n-1)(2n+1)(2n+3)(2n+5)}{64}$, then $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{r=1}^{n}\left(\dfrac{1}{T_r}\right)$ is equal to:
problem_types: find Tn from Sn then sum reciprocal series using telescoping
common_mistakes: Errors in finding Tn = Sn - Sn-1
Incorrect partial fraction decomposition of 1/Tr
prerequisite_concepts: relation between sum of series and its general term

subject: Mathematics
question_text: From all the English alphabets, five letters are chosen and arranged in alphabetical order. The total number of ways, in which the middle letter is 'M', is:
problem_types: count selections with a fixed middle element under ordering constraint
common_mistakes: Wrong count of letters before/after 'M' (12 before, 13 after)
Using permutations instead of combinations since order is forced alphabetical
prerequisite_concepts: position of 'M' in the alphabet (13th letter)

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let $x = x(y)$ be the solution of the differential equation $y^2\,dx + \left(x - \dfrac{1}{y}\right)dy = 0$. If $x(1) = 1$, then $x\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ is:
problem_types: solve linear ODE in x as function of y and evaluate at a point
common_mistakes: Incorrect integrating factor $e^{-1/y}$
Sign/substitution errors with $t = -1/y$ while integrating $\int t e^t dt$

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let the parabola $y = x^2 + px - 3$ meet the coordinate axes at the points P, Q and R. If the circle C with centre $(-1,-1)$ passes through the points P, Q and R, then the area of $\triangle PQR$ is:
problem_types: find p using circle passing through axis-intercepts then compute area
common_mistakes: Not using that R=(0,-3) lies on the circle to find r^2
Sign error in determinant formula for area
prerequisite_concepts: x and y intercepts of a curve
equation of circle with given centre and radius

subject: Mathematics
question_text: A circle C of radius 2 lies in the second quadrant and touches both the coordinate axes. Let r be the radius of a circle that has centre at the point $(2,5)$ and intersects the circle C at exactly two points. If the set of all possible values of r is the interval $(\alpha, \beta)$, then $3\beta - 2\alpha$ is equal to:
concept_tags: condition for two circles to intersect at two points
problem_types: find range of radius for two circles intersecting at two points
common_mistakes: Wrong centre of circle C (should be (-2,2) for second quadrant touching both axes)
Using non-strict inequalities instead of the open interval condition $|r_1-r_2| < d < r_1+r_2$
prerequisite_concepts: circle touching both axes has centre (±r,±r)

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let for $f(x) = 7\tan^8 x + 7\tan^6 x - 3\tan^4 x - 3\tan^2 x$, $I_1 = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4} f(x)\,dx$ and $I_2 = \displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/4} x f(x)\,dx$. Then $7I_1 + 12I_2$ is equal to:
problem_types: evaluate combination of two definite integrals using substitution and IBP
common_mistakes: Not recognizing f(x)=(7tan^6x-3tan^2x)sec^2x for substitution t=tan x
Errors applying integration by parts for I2
prerequisite_concepts: evaluating I1 first to simplify I2

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let $f(x)$ be a real differentiable function such that $f(0) = 1$ and $f(x+y) = f(x)f'(y) + f'(x)f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$. Then $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{100}\log_e f(n)$ is equal to:
problem_types: derive f(x)=e^{x/2} from functional equation and sum logs
common_mistakes: Errors substituting x=y=0 to find f'(0)
Forgetting f(0)=1 gives integration constant C=0
prerequisite_concepts: sum of first n natural numbers

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let $A = \{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 10\}$ and $B = \left\{\dfrac{m}{n} : m, n \in A, m < n \text{ and } \gcd(m,n) = 1\right\}$. Then $n(B)$ is equal to:
problem_types: count distinct fractions m/n with m<n and gcd(m,n)=1
common_mistakes: Double counting fractions that reduce to the same value (e.g. 2/4 = 1/2)
Missing some coprime pairs while enumerating each denominator

subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Area Under Curves - Circle and Parabola
question_text: The area of the region, inside the circle $(x - 2\sqrt{3})^2 + y^2 = 12$ and outside the parabola $y^2 = 2\sqrt{3}x$, is:
problem_types: find area inside circle and outside parabola using integration
common_mistakes: Not using symmetry about the x-axis correctly (factor of 2)
Errors finding limits of intersection of circle and parabola

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Two balls are selected at random one by one without replacement from a bag containing 4 white and 6 black balls. If the probability that the first selected ball is black, given that the second selected ball is also black, is $\dfrac{m}{n}$, where $\gcd(m,n) = 1$, then $m+n$ is equal to:
problem_types: find P(first black | second black) using Bayes' theorem
common_mistakes: Confusing P(second black|first black) with the required reverse conditional
Forgetting to compute total P(second ball black) over both cases (first white or black)

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let the foci of a hyperbola be $(1, 14)$ and $(1, -12)$. If it passes through the point $(1, 6)$, then the length of its latus-rectum is:
problem_types: find hyperbola parameters from foci and a point on it
common_mistakes: Confusing 'be' (distance from centre to focus) with 'a' directly
Sign error finding b^2 = b^2e^2 - b^2 = a^2(e^2-1)

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} -3ax^2 - 2, & x < 1 \\ a^2 + bx, & x \ge 1 \end{cases}$ be differentiable for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$, where $a > 1$, $b \in \mathbb{R}$. If the area of the region enclosed by $y = f(x)$ and the line $y = -20$ is $\alpha + \beta\sqrt{3}$, $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{Z}$, then the value of $\alpha + \beta$ is ____.
problem_types: find unknown parameters using differentiability then compute enclosed area
common_mistakes: Using only continuity and not matching derivatives (LHD=RHD) to get both equations for a and b
Errors finding x-intercepts of intersection with y=-20 involving sqrt(3)
prerequisite_concepts: continuity and differentiability at a junction point
definite integration to find enclosed area

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let $\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{5}\dfrac{{}^{11}C_{2r+1}}{2r+2} = \dfrac{m}{n}$, $\gcd(m,n) = 1$. Then $m - n$ is equal to ____.
problem_types: evaluate sum of binomial coefficients divided by index using integration trick
common_mistakes: Not recognizing that integrating $(1+x)^{11}$ from 0 to 1 and -1 to 0 generates the required terms
Sign errors when integrating from -1 to 0

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let A be a square matrix of order 3 such that $\det(A) = -2$ and $\det\big(3\,\text{adj}(-6\,\text{adj}(3A))\big) = 2^{m+n}\cdot 3^{mn}$, $m > n$. Then $4m + 2n$ is equal to ____.
problem_types: repeatedly apply det(adj(A)) = det(A)^{n-1} and det(kA) = k^n det(A) for 3x3 matrix
common_mistakes: Wrong power used for det(adj(A)) for a 3x3 matrix (should be det(A)^2)
Forgetting the scalar factor (k^3) when computing det(kB) for 3x3 matrices
prerequisite_concepts: det(adj A) = det(A)^{n-1} for n x n matrix

subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Intersecting Lines and Foot of Perpendicular
question_text: Let $L_1: \dfrac{x-1}{3} = \dfrac{y-1}{-1} = \dfrac{z+1}{0}$ and $L_2: \dfrac{x-2}{2} = \dfrac{y}{0} = \dfrac{z+4}{\alpha}$, $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$, be two lines, which intersect at the point B. If P is the foot of perpendicular from the point $A(1, 1, -1)$ on $L_2$, then the value of $26\alpha(PB)^2$ is ____.
problem_types: find intersection point of two lines then compute foot of perpendicular and a distance
common_mistakes: Errors equating parametric coordinates from L1 and L2 to find the intersection point B
Sign/algebra mistakes finding the foot of perpendicular P using AP perpendicular to L2
prerequisite_concepts: solving for intersection of two lines in 3D
foot of perpendicular from a point to a line

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let $\vec{c}$ be the projection vector of $\vec{b} = \lambda\hat{i} + 4\hat{k}$, $\lambda > 0$, on the vector $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$. If $|\vec{a} + \vec{c}| = 7$, then the area of the parallelogram formed by the vectors $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ is ____.
problem_types: find lambda using projection vector magnitude condition then compute |b x c|
common_mistakes: Errors in the projection vector formula $\vec{c} = \left(\dfrac{\vec{b}\cdot\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|^2}\right)\vec{a}$
Arithmetic mistakes evaluating the 3x3 determinant for cross product
prerequisite_concepts: projection of a vector on another vector

subject: Physics
question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a vernier callipers, one vernier scale division is always smaller than one main scale division.

Statement II: The vernier constant is given by one main scale division multiplied by the number of vernier scale divisions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

problem_types: assertion-type statements on measuring instruments
common_mistakes: Assuming the vernier scale division is always smaller than the main scale division in every modified design
Confusing the formula for vernier constant (least count) with main scale division x number of divisions
prerequisite_concepts: least count = 1 MSD / number of VSD

subject: Physics
question_text: A line charge of length $\dfrac{a}{2}$ is kept at the center of an edge BC of a cube ABCDEFGH having edge length 'a' as shown in the figure. If the density of the line is $\lambda$ C per unit length, then the total electric flux through all the faces of the cube will be ____. (Take $\varepsilon_0$ as the free space permittivity)
problem_types: find flux through a cube due to a partially enclosed line charge along an edge
common_mistakes: Forgetting that only a fraction of the line charge lies inside the cube (the charge is symmetric about the edge, so only half the cube's worth contributes)
Not dividing the enclosed charge correctly based on geometry of the edge
prerequisite_concepts: symmetry arguments for charge enclosed by a Gaussian surface

subject: Physics
question_text: Sliding contact of a potentiometer is in the middle of the potentiometer wire having resistance $R_p = 1\,\Omega$ as shown in the figure. An external resistance of $R_e = 2\,\Omega$ is connected via the sliding contact, with an emf source of 0.9 V. The current in the circuit is:
problem_types: reduce a potentiometer circuit with sliding contact to an equivalent resistance and find current
common_mistakes: Not splitting the potentiometer wire resistance into two equal halves at the sliding contact
Incorrectly combining the half-wire resistances with Re in parallel/series
prerequisite_concepts: equivalent resistance for series and parallel combinations

subject: Physics
question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If Young's double slit experiment is performed in an optically denser medium than air, then the consecutive fringes come closer.

Reason (R): The speed of light reduces in an optically denser medium than air while its frequency does not change.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

problem_types: assertion-reason on fringe width dependence on medium
common_mistakes: Forgetting fringe width depends on wavelength in the medium, not in vacuum
Confusing the relation v = c/mu with frequency changing in a medium
prerequisite_concepts: fringe width beta = lambda D / d

subject: Physics
question_text: Two spherical bodies of the same material having radii 0.2 m and 0.8 m are placed in the same atmosphere. The temperature of the smaller body is 800 K and the temperature of the bigger body is 400 K. If the energy radiated from the smaller body is E, the energy radiated from the bigger body is (assume the effect of the surrounding to be negligible):
concept_tags: radiated power proportional to area and T^4
problem_types: compare radiated energy of two bodies given radius and temperature ratios
common_mistakes: Forgetting power depends on surface area (R^2), not just T^4
Errors in setting up the ratio (0.2/0.8)^2 x (800/400)^4
prerequisite_concepts: P proportional to A T^4 (Stefan's law)

subject: Physics
subtopic: Calorimetry - Latent Heat and Specific Heat
question_text: An amount of ice of mass $10^{-3}$ kg and temperature $-10^\circ C$ is transformed to vapour of temperature $110^\circ C$ by applying heat. The total amount of work required for this conversion is: (Take, specific heat of ice $= 2100\,Jkg^{-1}K^{-1}$, specific heat of water $= 4180\,Jkg^{-1}K^{-1}$, specific heat of steam $= 1920\,Jkg^{-1}K^{-1}$, latent heat of ice $= 3.35\times10^5\,Jkg^{-1}$ and latent heat of steam $= 2.25\times10^6\,Jkg^{-1}$)
problem_types: sum up heat required across five stages: heating ice, melting, heating water, vaporizing, heating steam
common_mistakes: Missing one of the five stages (e.g., heating the steam from 100C to 110C)
Using wrong mass units (not converting to kg consistently)

subject: Physics
subtopic: Bohr Model and de Broglie Wavelength
question_text: An electron in the ground state of the hydrogen atom has the orbital radius of $5.3\times10^{-11}$ m while that for the electron in the third excited state is $8.48\times10^{-10}$ m. The ratio of the de Broglie wavelengths of electron in the ground state to that in the excited state is:
problem_types: relate de Broglie wavelength ratio to orbital radius and quantum number ratio
common_mistakes: Forgetting that lambda is proportional to r/n, not just r
Using n=4 incorrectly for 'third excited state' (n should be 4 since ground state is n=1)

subject: Physics
subtopic: Power of Lens Combination - Refraction at Curved Surfaces
question_text: In the diagram given below, there are three lenses formed. Considering negligible thickness of each of them as compared to $|R_1|$ and $|R_2|$, i.e., the radii of curvature for the upper and lower surfaces of the glass lens, the power of the combination is:
problem_types: compute net power of a stack of water-glass-water refracting surfaces
common_mistakes: Using wrong sign convention for radii of curvature of upper vs lower surfaces
Forgetting to add powers of all three individual refracting surfaces (p1+p2+p3)
prerequisite_concepts: refraction formula at a single spherical surface (mu2/v - mu1/u = (mu2-mu1)/R)
power of combination = sum of individual powers

subject: Physics
subtopic: Motion of Charged Particle in Uniform Electric Field
question_text: An electron is made to enter symmetrically between two parallel and equally but oppositely charged metal plates, each of 10 cm length. The electron emerges out of the field region with a horizontal component of velocity $10^6$ m/s. If the magnitude of the electric field between the plates is 9.1 V/cm, then the vertical component of velocity of the electron is (mass of electron $= 9.1\times10^{-31}$ kg and charge of electron $= 1.6\times10^{-19}$ C):
problem_types: find vertical velocity component using time of flight and acceleration from electric field
common_mistakes: Not converting the electric field from V/cm to V/m
Using the wrong length/time relation t = l/v_x
prerequisite_concepts: time of flight t = horizontal length / horizontal velocity

subject: Physics
question_text: Which of the following resistivity ($\rho$) v/s temperature (T) curves is most suitable to be used in wire bound standard resistors?

options.text: Resistivity nearly constant, very slight positive slope with temperature
Resistivity increases sharply (concave up) with temperature
Resistivity decreases sharply then becomes nearly flat with temperature

problem_types: identify correct rho-T graph for a material property
common_mistakes: Choosing a curve where resistivity strongly depends on temperature, unsuitable for a 'standard' resistor
Confusing behaviour of metals (manganin/constantan, nearly temperature independent) with semiconductors
prerequisite_concepts: materials with near-zero temperature coefficient of resistivity used for standard resistors (e.g. manganin)

subject: Physics
question_text: A closed organ tube and an open organ tube filled by two different gases having the same bulk modulus but different densities $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ respectively. The frequency of the $9^{th}$ harmonic of the closed tube is identical with the $4^{th}$ harmonic of the open tube. If the length of the closed tube is 10 cm and the density ratio of the gases is $\rho_1 : \rho_2 = 1 : 16$, then the length of the open tube is:
concept_tags: harmonics in open and closed pipes
speed of sound in a gas
problem_types: equate harmonic frequencies of closed and open pipes with different gas densities
common_mistakes: Using wrong harmonic formulas (closed pipe only supports odd harmonics: n=2k-1; open pipe supports all harmonics)
Forgetting speed of sound v = sqrt(B/rho) depends on the gas density

subject: Physics
subtopic: Moment of Inertia of a Disc with a Cut-out
question_text: A uniform circular disc of radius 'R' and mass 'M' is rotating about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through its centre. A small circular part of radius $R/2$ is removed from the original disc as shown in the figure. Find the moment of inertia of the remaining part of the original disc about the axis as given above.
problem_types: find moment of inertia of a disc with a circular cavity using subtraction method
common_mistakes: Using wrong mass for the removed disc (should be M/4, proportional to area)
Forgetting to apply the parallel axis theorem for the removed piece's own axis vs the main axis
prerequisite_concepts: I of a disc about its centre = MR^2/2
parallel axis theorem I = Icm + Md^2
mass scales with area for uniform discs

subject: Physics
subtopic: Gravitational Force due to a Sphere with a Cavity
question_text: A small point of mass m is placed at a distance 2R from the centre 'O' of a big uniform solid sphere of mass M and radius R. The gravitational force on 'm' due to M is $F_1$. A spherical part of radius $R/3$ is removed from the big sphere as shown in the figure and the gravitational force on m due to the remaining part of M is found to be $F_2$. The value of the ratio $F_1 : F_2$ is:
problem_types: use superposition (whole sphere minus removed cavity) to find gravitational force
common_mistakes: Wrong mass of removed spherical cavity (mass scales with volume, M/27 for radius R/3)
Wrong distance of the cavity's centre from the point mass m
prerequisite_concepts: mass proportional to r^3 for uniform density

subject: Physics
topic: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
question_text: The work functions of cesium (Cs) and lithium (Li) metals are 1.9 eV and 2.5 eV, respectively. If we incident a light of wavelength 550 nm on these two metal surfaces, then photoelectric effect is possible for the case of:
problem_types: compare photon energy to work function to determine if photoemission occurs
common_mistakes: Using E=1240/lambda(nm) incorrectly (units mismatch)
Comparing photon energy to the wrong metal's work function
prerequisite_concepts: photoelectric effect occurs only if photon energy >= work function

subject: Physics
question_text: If B is the magnetic field and $\mu_0$ is the permeability of free space, then the dimensions of $(B/\mu_0)$ is:
problem_types: dimensional formula
common_mistakes: Forgetting B = mu0 n i so B/mu0 has the dimensions of (turns per length x current) = [L^-1 A]
Trying to derive dimensions of B and mu0 separately from unrelated formulas
prerequisite_concepts: B = mu0 n i for a solenoid
dimensional formula of current and length

subject: Physics
question_text: A bob of mass m is suspended at a point O by a light string of length $l$ and left to perform vertical motion (circular) as shown in figure. Initially, by applying horizontal velocity $v_0$ at the point 'A', the string becomes slack when the bob reaches at the point 'D'. The ratio of the kinetic energy of the bob at the points B and C is ____.
problem_types: use slack-string condition at D to find v0, then apply energy conservation to find KE at B and C
common_mistakes: Using the slack condition (mg=mv^2/l, i.e. v_D^2=gl) at the wrong point
Errors computing height differences of B and C relative to A
prerequisite_concepts: condition for string to become slack: v^2=gl at the point

subject: Physics
subtopic: Cells in Parallel - Equivalent EMF and Internal Resistance
question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement-I: The equivalent emf of two nonideal batteries connected in parallel is smaller than either of the two emfs.

Statement-II: The equivalent internal resistance of two nonideal batteries connected in parallel is smaller than the internal resistance of either of the two batteries.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true

problem_types: assertion-type comparison of equivalent emf and resistance for parallel cells
common_mistakes: Assuming equivalent emf in parallel is always smaller than both individual emfs (it actually lies between them)
Not knowing the formula for equivalent emf and resistance of cells in parallel
prerequisite_concepts: equivalent resistance of resistors in parallel is less than the smallest individual resistance

subject: Physics
question_text: Which of the following circuits represents a forward biased diode? (Circuits A to E are shown with different applied voltages on either side of a diode.)
problem_types: identify forward-biased diode circuits from given p-n orientation and voltage values
common_mistakes: Not noting the orientation (direction) of the diode symbol in each circuit
Comparing voltages without considering which terminal is p-side and which is n-side
prerequisite_concepts: forward bias: p-side at higher potential than n-side

subject: Physics
question_text: A parallel-plate capacitor of capacitance $40\mu F$ is connected to a 100 V power supply. Now the intermediate space between the plates is filled with a dielectric material of dielectric constant $K = 2$. Due to the introduction of the dielectric material, the extra charge and the change in the electrostatic energy in the capacitor, respectively, are:
problem_types: find extra charge and change in stored energy when dielectric is inserted at constant voltage
common_mistakes: Using Q=CV with original C instead of new C=KC for the new charge
Sign error or factor error computing ΔU = (1/2)(K-1)CV^2

subject: Physics
question_text: Given is a thin convex lens of glass (refractive index $\mu$) and each side having radius of curvature R. One side is polished for complete reflection. At what distance from the lens, an object be placed on the optic axis so that the image gets formed on the object itself?
problem_types: find equivalent focal length of a silvered plano-convex/biconvex lens system
common_mistakes: Forgetting the silvered surface acts as a mirror, so light passes through the lens twice (P_eq = 2P_lens + P_mirror)
Sign errors in radius of curvature for the mirror term

subject: Physics
question_text: Two soap bubbles of radius 2 cm and 4 cm, respectively, are in contact with each other. The radius of curvature of the common surface, in cm, is ____.
concept_tags: excess pressure in a soap bubble
problem_types: find radius of curvature of common interface between two soap bubbles
common_mistakes: Using r1+r2 instead of r1*r2/(r1-r2)
Sign confusion regarding which bubble is larger
prerequisite_concepts: excess pressure inside a soap bubble = 4T/r
pressure balance at the common interface gives r = r1 r2 / (r1 - r2)

subject: Physics
question_text: The driver sitting inside a parked car is watching vehicles approaching from behind with the help of his side view mirror, which is a convex mirror with radius of curvature $R = 2$ m. Another car approaches him from behind with a uniform speed of 90 km/hr. When the car is at a distance of 24 m from him, the magnitude of the acceleration of the image of the side view mirror is 'a'. The value of 100a is ____ $m/s^2$.
problem_types: find acceleration of image by differentiating mirror formula twice with respect to time
common_mistakes: Forgetting to differentiate the mirror formula twice (once for velocity, once for acceleration of image)
Sign errors in u, v conventions for a convex mirror
prerequisite_concepts: differentiating implicit relations with respect to time

subject: Physics
subtopic: Heat Conduction - Series and Parallel Combinations
question_text: Three conductors of same length having thermal conductivity $k_1$, $k_2$ and $k_3$ are connected as shown in the figure. Area of cross sections of the $1^{st}$ and $2^{nd}$ conductor are same and for the $3^{rd}$ conductor it is double of the $1^{st}$ conductor. The temperatures are given in the figure ($100^\circ C$, $\theta^\circ C$, $0^\circ C$). In steady state condition, the value of $\theta$ is ____ $^\circ C$. (Given: $k_1 = 60$, $k_2 = 120$, $k_3 = 135\,Js^{-1}m^{-1}K^{-1}$)
problem_types: find junction temperature using thermal resistance network in steady state
common_mistakes: Wrong thermal resistance formula R=L/(kA) - forgetting the factor of area for the 3rd conductor
Treating the parallel combination of k1,k2 incorrectly while combining with k3 in series
prerequisite_concepts: heat current analogy with electrical current (series/parallel combination)

subject: Physics
subtopic: Angular Momentum of a Particle about Another Particle
question_text: The position vectors of two 1 kg particles, (A) and (B), are given by $\vec{r}_A = (\alpha_1 t^2\hat{i} + \alpha_2 t\hat{j} + \alpha_3 t\hat{k})$ m and $\vec{r}_B = (\beta_1 t\hat{i} + \beta_2 t^2\hat{j} + \beta_3 t\hat{k})$ m, respectively; ($\alpha_1 = 1\,m/s^2$, $\alpha_2 = 3n\,m/s$, $\alpha_3 = 2\,m/s$, $\beta_1 = 2\,m/s$, $\beta_2 = -1\,m/s^2$, $\beta_3 = 4p\,m/s$), where t is time, and n and p are constants. At $t = 1s$, $|\vec{V}_A| = |\vec{V}_B|$ and the velocities $\vec{V}_A$ and $\vec{V}_B$ of the particles are orthogonal to each other. At $t = 1$ s, the magnitude of the angular momentum of particle (A) with respect to the position of particle (B) is $\sqrt{L}$ kg m$^2$s$^{-1}$. The value of L is ____.
problem_types: find unknown constants from velocity conditions, then compute angular momentum L = m(r_A/B x V_A)
common_mistakes: Errors differentiating position vectors to get velocity vectors
Sign errors solving the simultaneous equations from |VA|=|VB| and VA.VB=0
prerequisite_concepts: angular momentum L = m (r x v)

subject: Physics
subtopic: Projectile Motion - Distance in nth Second
question_text: A particle is projected at an angle of $30^\circ$ from horizontal at a speed of 60 m/s. The height traversed by the particle in the first second is $h_0$ and the height traversed in the last second, before it reaches the maximum height, is $h_1$. The ratio $h_0 : h_1$ is ____. [Take, $g = 10\,m/s^2$]
problem_types: find ratio of distances traveled in first and last seconds of upward motion
common_mistakes: Forgetting to use the 'distance in nth second' formula S_n = u - g(2n-1)/2 with appropriate sign for the last second of ascent
Incorrectly computing total time to reach maximum height
prerequisite_concepts: S_n = ut - (1/2)gt^2 applied for the nth second
time to reach maximum height = u_y/g
